shortTerm.summary: A House of Commons Library briefing on the UK's small charity sector (96% of the UK's 165,758 voluntary organisations) cites Charities Aid Foundation data showing individual giving down to 50% of people donating (from 58% in 2019), roughly four million fewer donors, plus reduced government funding and an estimated £1.4bn added National Insurance burden from October 2024 changes.

longTerm.summary: Legacy Foresight's charity legacy income forecasts project UK legacy giving reaching £5 billion annually by 2030 (up from £3bn in 2020), with an estimated £23 billion in cumulative legacy income over 2026-2030 and 146,000 bequests expected in 2030, driven by Baby Boomer wealth and demographics; legacy incomes are projected to double again in real terms by 2050. This long-term legacy-giving growth partly offsets near-term declines in individual cash donations.

risks: Declining individual donor base (down from 58% to 50% of the public)
Reduced government funding and lack of multi-year unrestricted grants
Added National Insurance costs from October 2024 changes (~£1.4bn sector-wide)
opportunities: Doubled Employment Allowance (to £10,500) partly offsetting NI cost increases
NCVO and sector bodies pushing for improved funding systems and representation
Legacy giving forecast to reach £5bn annually by 2030 and double again in real terms by 2050, driven by Baby Boomer wealth transfer
